TestTopology::test_crash_during_decommis.description: 3-node cluster (RBNO forced for bootstrap/decommission to slow ops), decommission node1 in a background thread while repeatedly hard-killing/restarting node2 (up to 10 times, then waits for decommission to fail). Asserts `nodetool status` on node2 has no ' null ' entry after 30s sleep. Ported from Cassandra test for CASSANDRA-10231 (null status entries for decommissioned node after crash).

origin.summary: Cassandra dtest reproducing CASSANDRA-10231; enabled for scylla in fcc77da925 (PR #387). PR #52 in data is the upstream merge.

TestTopology::test_crash_during_decommis.relevance: Decommission + node crash still live, but the asserted symptom (' null ' in nodetool status) is Cassandra Java-nodetool output. ccm runs native `scylla nodetool` (scylla-ccm/ccmlib/scylla_node.py:961), whose status prints '?' for unknown host id/load (tools/scylla-nodetool.cc ~2878-2897), never 'null'.

TestTopology::test_crash_during_decommis.reason: Cassandra-specific assertion (CASSANDRA-10231 'null' status entry) that can't fail with native scylla nodetool (never prints 'null'); the ' null ' early-break in the loop is also dead, so the test just kills node2 up to 10x. Slow (~84s), timing-fragile (dtest#3962, #5310, f2a821f4d0); decommission failure/crash handling is covered deterministically by test/cluster tests listed.

issues.text: ' null ' status assert can't fail: native scylla nodetool never prints 'null' (Cassandra CASSANDRA-10231 symptom).
' null ' early-break in the kill loop is dead; loop always kills node2 up to 10x.
